text:
Beautiful nymphs, who dwell within the river,

content in homes built out of gleaming stones

and held aloft on columns made of glass,


whether you now weave, absorbed in your work,

or fashion delicate cloth,

or whether, set apart from one another,

you tell of loves and lives;


leave your work awhile, lift up

your golden heads to look at me,

and you will not detain yourselves long, as I fare,


for either pity will keep you from hearing me,

or, turned to water here by weeping,

you may console me there at leisure.

translation.title: Sonnet XI
